findings.description: Unsafe deserialization using pickle.loads() on user-supplied meta data in Style class allows arbitrary code execution
findings.reasoning: The code uses `pickle.loads()` to deserialize the `_meta` field which is populated from user-supplied `meta` parameter in the constructor (line 196: `self._meta = None if meta is None else dumps(meta)`). The `meta` parameter is accepted as a Dict[str, Any] from callers like `Style.from_meta()` and can contain arbitrary Python objects. When `pickle.loads()` deserializes a malicious pickle payload, it will execute arbitrary code during deserialization.

evidence.code_context: The Style class accepts a 'meta' parameter in __init__ (line 144) and from_meta() class method (line 233). This meta dict is serialized using pickle.dumps() and stored in _meta field. When the meta property is accessed (line 471), it deserializes using pickle.loads(), which can execute arbitrary code.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: User supplies meta dict → Style.__init__(meta=...) or Style.from_meta(meta=...) → pickle.dumps(meta) stored in self._meta → pickle.loads(self._meta) in meta property → Code execution
evidence.notes: pickle.loads() is inherently unsafe with untrusted data. The imports show: 'from pickle import dumps, loads' at line 4. This is a vendor directory (pip/_vendor/rich/), but the vulnerability is still exploitable if an attacker can influence the meta parameter passed to Style objects.
